title: Why Falling Birth Rates Will Be a Bigger Problem Than Overpopulation

mock_data.title: Why Falling Birth Rates Will Be a Bigger Problem Than Overpopulation
mock_data.passage:
Think of global population problems and you might think of the growing number of people in the world – currently about 8 billion – and our collective toll on the planet. But due to people having fewer children as countries become more prosperous, the real demographic problem may turn out to be falling populations.

Projecting from current trends, demographers have now predicted that, within about 25 years, three-quarters of countries will have birth rates that are too low to maintain their populations. While this may be good news for the environment, having fewer working-age people to support those who are older presents a huge economic challenge.

The latest projections also indicate that there will be a sharp divide between countries with low birth rates and generally high incomes – such as most European nations – and a smaller number of countries, mainly in Africa, with higher birth rates and low incomes.

"We are facing staggering social change through the 21st Century," researcher Stein Emil Vollset at the University of Washington in Seattle said in a statement. "The world will be simultaneously tackling a baby boom in some countries and a baby bust in others."

Maintaining economic and societal stability in the face of these stark differences will be one of the key challenges of this century. So what should countries be doing to prepare for this demographic time bomb?

While the trend of a rising global population has long caused environmental concerns, demographers also knew it wouldn't continue indefinitely. Estimates vary, but we seem on course to hit "peak people" sometime between 2060 and 2080, with a head count of 9.5 to 10 billion people, falling thereafter.

The latest projections from Vollset's team are broadly in line with previous predictions from bodies such as the United Nations in terms of global trends. What is new is a more detailed breakdown of how things will change country by country, based on the latest data on birth rates for five-year age groups from those aged between 10 and 54, projected to the year 2100.

Countries generally require a birth rate of 2.1 children per woman for their populations to stay constant. Vollset's team found that, by 2050, the birth rate will have fallen below this level in 76 per cent of countries. By 2100, this is forecast to reach 97 per cent.

At the same time, people are living longer, so populations as a whole have fewer people of working age who can provide for older people and others who are economically inactive. An ageing population cannot be avoided, says Vegard Skirbekk at the Norwegian Institute of Public Health in Oslo. "However, one should try to make the transition slow in order to better be able to prepare for this process."

To slow falling birth rates, high-income countries should attempt to make it easier and more attractive for people to have more children, for instance by improving access to housing and fertility treatments, says Skirbekk.

Countries also need to plan to cope with their shrinking and ageing populations by building more hospitals, updating transport systems and having fewer schools, says Melinda Mills at the University of Oxford. "Cities are focusing on getting people to schools and to work. They might have to focus more on getting them to shops and hospitals," she says.

Jennifer Sciubba at the Wilson Center, a think tank in Washington DC, says companies also need to make it easier for older people to stay in work for longer, for instance, on reduced hours. "We have this binary view that you're either working or not, but that doesn't have to be the case," she says.

A minority of countries, however, face the opposite challenge of having a higher birth rate than the 2.1 replacement level. The new study finds this will probably still be true even in 2100. Most such nations will be in sub-Saharan Africa and are projected to account for one in every two children born in 2100.

In these countries, better access to contraception and education for girls have been shown to reduce birth rates, says Sciubba. Migration from high-birth-rate and low-income countries is also likely to continue, which could lead to competition between richer countries for migrants from sub-Saharan Africa, the authors of the new study say in their paper. "However, this approach will only work if there is a shift in current public and political attitudes towards immigration," they say.
mock_data.passageB1:
When you think about the world's population, you might think about the number of people increasing. There are about 8 billion people now, and we use a lot of the Earth's resources. But, because people in richer countries are having fewer children, the real problem might be that populations are decreasing.

Experts who study populations say that in about 25 years, most countries will not have enough babies being born to keep the population the same. This might be good for the Earth, but it means there will be fewer people of working age to support older people. This will be a big economic problem.

The latest predictions show that there will be a big difference between countries. Many European countries will have low birth rates and high incomes. But some countries, mostly in Africa, will have higher birth rates and low incomes.

A researcher named Stein Emil Vollset said that the world will see big social changes in the 21st century. Some countries will have a lot of babies, and others will have very few.

It will be hard to keep the economy and society stable with these big differences. So, countries need to prepare for this problem.

People have been worried about the world's population growing too much. But experts knew that it wouldn't keep growing forever. It seems that the number of people in the world will peak around 2060 or 2080, with about 9.5 to 10 billion people. After that, the population will start to fall.

Vollset's team's predictions are like other predictions from groups like the United Nations. But the new predictions give more details about how things will change in each country. They looked at the latest information about birth rates for women between 10 and 54 years old, and they made predictions until the year 2100.

Usually, a country needs women to have about 2.1 children each to keep the population the same. Vollset's team found that by 2050, most countries will have birth rates lower than this. By 2100, they think almost all countries will have this problem.

At the same time, people are living longer. This means there are fewer people of working age to take care of older people and others who are not working. Vegard Skirbekk says that we can't stop the population from getting older. But we should try to make the change slow so we can get ready for it.

To make birth rates go up, rich countries should try to make it easier for people to have children. For example, they could help people find housing and get help with having babies, says Skirbekk.

Countries also need to plan for smaller and older populations. They need to build more hospitals, improve transportation, and have fewer schools, says Melinda Mills. Cities might need to focus more on helping people get to shops and hospitals.

Jennifer Sciubba says that companies should make it easier for older people to keep working, even if it's only for a few hours a week. She says that we think people are either working or not, but that doesn't have to be true.

However, some countries will have the opposite problem: birth rates that are too high. The study says this will still be true in 2100. Most of these countries will be in Africa. They will probably have half of all the babies born in 2100.

In these countries, giving women better access to contraception and education can help lower birth rates, says Sciubba. People from countries with high birth rates and low incomes will probably move to other countries. This could make richer countries compete for people from Africa. But, the study says this will only work if people start to feel differently about immigration.

It is important to address these challenges now to ensure a more stable and prosperous future for everyone.

Governments and organizations need to work together to find solutions that work for each country's unique situation. This includes investing in education, healthcare, and social programs that support families and help people adapt to changing demographics.

Ultimately, the goal is to create a world where everyone has the opportunity to thrive, regardless of their age or where they live. By working together, we can overcome the challenges of falling birth rates and create a better future for all.

However, because people are having fewer children as countries become wealthier, the real problem in the future might be declining populations. This could have significant consequences for societies and economies worldwide.

Based on current trends, experts predict that in about 25 years, most countries (around three-quarters) will have birth rates that are too low to maintain their current population size. While this could be seen as a positive development for the environment, a smaller working-age population supporting a larger elderly population presents a major economic challenge. It's a complex situation with both advantages and disadvantages.

New research suggests a clear division will emerge between countries with low birth rates and generally high incomes, like most of Europe, and a smaller group of countries, mostly in Africa, with higher birth rates and lower incomes. This divergence in demographic trends will require different approaches to policy and planning.

The world will be simultaneously dealing with a baby boom in some countries and a baby bust in others." This highlights the complexity of the situation and the need for careful planning.

Maintaining economic and social stability in the face of these stark contrasts will be a key challenge this century. So, what steps should countries take to prepare for this demographic shift? It's crucial to consider the potential impacts and develop appropriate strategies.

While the long-term trend of a rising global population has raised environmental concerns, demographers have always known that this growth wouldn't continue forever. Estimates vary, but it seems we are on track to reach "peak people" sometime between 2060 and 2080, with a global population of 9.5 to 10 billion, after which it will start to fall. This plateauing of population growth is a significant turning point.

However, the new research provides a more detailed analysis of how things will change from country to country, based on the latest data on birth rates for five-year age groups between 10 and 54, projected to the year 2100. This level of detail is crucial for effective planning.

Vollset's team found that by 2050, the birth rate will have fallen below this level in 76% of countries. By 2100, this is forecast to reach 97%. This widespread decline in birth rates presents a significant challenge for many nations.

At the same time, people are living longer, meaning that populations have fewer working-age people to support older people and others who are not working. An ageing population is inevitable, according to Vegard Skirbekk at the Norwegian Institute of Public Health in Oslo. "However, one should try to make the transition slow in order to better be able to prepare for this process." A gradual transition is easier to manage than a rapid one.

To slow down falling birth rates, high-income countries should try to make it easier and more appealing for people to have more children. This could involve improving access to affordable housing and fertility treatments, says Skirbekk. Supportive policies can make a difference.

Countries also need to plan for shrinking and ageing populations by building more hospitals, improving transport systems, and potentially having fewer schools, says Melinda Mills at the University of Oxford. "Cities are focusing on getting people to schools and to work. They might have to focus more on getting them to shops and hospitals," she says. "We have this binary view that you're either working or not, but that doesn't have to be the case," she says. Flexible work arrangements can help retain experienced workers.

Most of these countries will be in sub-Saharan Africa and are projected to account for half of all children born in 2100. The demographic challenges in these regions are very different.

Migration from high-birth-rate, low-income countries is also likely to continue, which could lead to richer countries competing for migrants from sub-Saharan Africa, according to the study's authors. "However, this approach will only work if there is a shift in current public and political attitudes towards immigration," they say. Changing attitudes and policies will be essential for managing migration effectively.

Moreover, migration from high-birth-rate, low-income countries is expected to persist, potentially leading to increased competition among wealthier nations for migrants from sub-Saharan Africa. However, the study authors emphasize that the success of such an approach is contingent on a fundamental shift in public and political attitudes towards immigration. A more nuanced understanding of the benefits and challenges of migration is crucial for fostering inclusive and sustainable societies.

mock_data.translation:
Global aholi muammolari haqida o'ylang va siz dunyodagi o'sib borayotgan odamlar soni – hozirda taxminan 8 milliard – va sayyoramizga umumiy ta'sirimiz haqida o'ylashingiz mumkin. Ammo mamlakatlar farovonroq bo'lgan sari odamlar kamroq farzand ko'rganligi sababli, haqiqiy demografik muammo aholining kamayishi bo'lishi mumkin.

Joriy tendentsiyalardan bashorat qilib, demograflar endi taxminan 25 yil ichida mamlakatlarning to'rtdan uch qismi aholini saqlab turish uchun juda past tug'ilish darajalariga ega bo'lishini bashorat qildilar. Bu atrof-muhit uchun yaxshi yangilik bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, keksalarni qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun mehnat yoshidagi odamlarning kamroq bo'lishi katta iqtisodiy qiyinchilik tug'diradi.

So'nggi bashoratlar, shuningdek, past tug'ilish darajalari va umuman yuqori daromadli mamlakatlar – ko'pgina Yevropa davlatlari kabi – va yuqoriroq tug'ilish darajalari va past daromadli, asosan Afrikadagi kamroq mamlakatlar o'rtasida keskin bo'linish bo'lishini ko'rsatadi.

"Biz 21-asr davomida hayratlanarli ijtimoiy o'zgarishlarga duch kelmoqdamiz," dedi Sietldagi Vashington universitetining tadqiqotchisi Stein Emil Vollset bayonotida. "Dunyo ba'zi mamlakatlarda chaqaloqlar portlashi va boshqalarida chaqaloqlar kamayishi bilan bir vaqtda kurashishi kerak bo'ladi."

Ushbu keskin farqlar sharoitida iqtisodiy va ijtimoiy barqarorlikni saqlab turish ushbu asrning asosiy qiyinchiliklaridan biri bo'ladi. Xo'sh, mamlakatlar ushbu demografik vaqtli bombaga tayyorgarlik ko'rish uchun nima qilishlari kerak?

O'sib borayotgan global aholi tendentsiyasi uzoq vaqtdan beri ekologik tashvishlarni keltirib chiqargan bo'lsa-da, demograflar bu cheksiz davom etmasligini ham bilishgan. Taxminlar turlicha, lekin biz 2060 va 2080 yillar oralig'ida 9,5 dan 10 milliard gacha odam bilan "eng yuqori aholi"ga erishish yo'lida ko'rinamiz, keyin esa pasayadi.

Vollset jamoasining so'nggi bashoratlari global tendentsiyalar bo'yicha Birlashgan Millatlar Tashkiloti kabi tashkilotlarning oldingi bashoratlari bilan keng ma'noda mos keladi. Yangilik shundaki, bu 10 dan 54 yoshgacha bo'lganlar orasida besh yillik yosh guruhlari bo'yicha tug'ilish darajalariga oid so'nggi ma'lumotlarga asoslanib, 2100-yilga qadar bashorat qilingan, mamlakat bo'yicha narsalar qanday o'zgarishining batafsil tahlili.

Mamlakatlar odatda aholini barqaror saqlash uchun har bir ayolga 2,1 ta bolani tug'ilish darajasi sifatida talab qiladi. Vollset jamoasi 2050-yilga kelib mamlakatlarning 76 foizida tug'ilish darajasi bu darajadan pastga tushishini aniqladi. 2100-yilga kelib bu 97 foizga yetishi bashorat qilinmoqda.

Shu bilan birga, odamlar uzoqroq yashaydilar, shuning uchun aholining ko'p qismi keksalar va iqtisodiy jihatdan faol bo'lmaganlarni ta'minlay oladigan mehnat yoshidagi odamlarning kamroq qismiga ega. Keksaygan aholidan qochib bo'lmaydi, deydi Oslodagi Norvegiya Jamoat salomatligi institutidagi Vegard Skirbekk. "Biroq, bu jarayonga yaxshiroq tayyorgarlik ko'rish uchun o'tishni sekinlashtrishga harakat qilish kerak."

Tug'ilish darajalarining pasayishini sekinlashtirish uchun yuqori daromadli mamlakatlar odamlar uchun ko'proq farzand ko'rishni osonlashtirish va jozibadorroq qilishga harakat qilishlari kerak, masalan, uy-joy va fertillik davolashga kirishni yaxshilash orqali, deydi Skirbekk.

Mamlakatlar, shuningdek, qisqaruvchi va keksaygan aholilari bilan kurashishni rejalashtirishlari kerak – ko'proq kasalxonalar qurish, transport tizimlarini yangilash va kamroq maktablarga ega bo'lish orqali, deydi Oksford universitetidagi Melinda Mills. "Shaharlar odamlarni maktablar va ishga olib borishga e'tibor qaratmoqda. Ular odamlarni do'konlar va kasalxonalarga olib borishga ko'proq e'tibor berishlari kerak bo'lishi mumkin," deydi u.

Vashingtondagi Wilson markazidagi tadqiqotchi Jennifer Sciubba kompaniyalar ham keksa odamlar uchun ishda uzoqroq qolishni osonlashtirishlari kerakligini aytadi, masalan, qisqartirilgan soatlar bilan. "Bizda siz yoki ishlaysiz yoki yo'q degan ikkilik ko'rinish bor, lekin bu shunday bo'lishi shart emas," deydi u.

Biroq, kamchilik mamlakatlar 2,1 almashtirish darajasidan yuqori tug'ilish darajasiga ega bo'lishning qarama-qarshi muammosiga duch keladi. Yangi tadqiqot bu 2100-yilda ham hali ham to'g'ri bo'lishi mumkinligini aniqladi. Bunday mamlakatlarning aksariyati sub-Sahara Afrikasida bo'ladi va 2100-yilda tug'ilgan har ikki boladan biriga to'g'ri kelishi bashorat qilinmoqda.

Bu mamlakatlarda qizlar uchun kontratseptsiyaga va ta'limga yaxshiroq kirish tug'ilish darajalarini pasaytirganligi ko'rsatilgan, deydi Sciubba. Yuqori tug'ilish darajali va past daromadli mamlakatlardan migratsiya ham davom etishi ehtimoldan yiroq emas, bu boyroq mamlakatlar orasida sub-Sahara Afrikasidan muhojirlar uchun raqobatga olib kelishi mumkin, deydi yangi tadqiqot mualliflari o'z maqolalarida. "Biroq, bu yondashuv faqat immigratsiyaga bo'lgan hozirgi jamoat va siyosiy munosabatlarda o'zgarish bo'lsa ishlaydi," deydi ular.

mock_data.translationB1:
Dunyodagi aholi haqida o'ylaganingizda, odamlar soni ko'payishi haqida o'ylashingiz mumkin. Hozirda taxminan 8 milliard odam bor va biz Yerning resurslaridan juda ko'p foydalanamiz. Ammo, boy mamlakatlarda odamlar kamroq farzand ko'rayotgani sababli, haqiqiy muammo aholi sonining kamayishi bo'lishi mumkin.

Aholi sonini o'rganuvchi ekspertlarning aytishicha, taxminan 25 yildan so'ng, ko'pchilik mamlakatlarda aholi sonini bir xilda saqlash uchun yetarli chaqaloqlar tug'ilmaydi. Bu Yer uchun yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin, ammo bu keksa odamlarni qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun ishlaydigan yoshdagi odamlar kamroq bo'lishini anglatadi. Bu katta iqtisodiy muammo bo'ladi.

Eng so'nggi prognozlar mamlakatlar o'rtasida katta farq bo'lishini ko'rsatmoqda. Ko'pgina Yevropa mamlakatlarida tug'ilish darajasi past va daromadlari yuqori bo'ladi. Ammo ba'zi mamlakatlarda, asosan Afrikada, tug'ilish darajasi yuqori va daromadlari past bo'ladi.

Stein Emil Vollset ismli tadqiqotchi 21-asrda dunyo katta ijtimoiy o'zgarishlarni ko'rishini aytdi. Ba'zi mamlakatlarda juda ko'p chaqaloqlar tug'iladi, boshqalarida esa juda kam.

Bu katta farqlar bilan iqtisodiyot va jamiyatni barqaror saqlash qiyin bo'ladi. Shunday qilib, mamlakatlar bu muammoga tayyorlanishi kerak.

Odamlar dunyo aholisining haddan tashqari o'sishidan xavotirda bo'lishgan. Ammo ekspertlar uning abadiy o'smay qolishini bilishardi. Ko'rinishidan, dunyo aholisi 2060 yoki 2080-yillarda eng yuqori cho'qqiga chiqadi, taxminan 9,5 dan 10 milliardgacha odam bo'ladi. Shundan so'ng, aholi soni kamayishni boshlaydi.

Vollset jamoasining prognozlari Birlashgan Millatlar Tashkiloti kabi guruhlarning boshqa prognozlariga o'xshaydi. Ammo yangi prognozlar har bir mamlakatda vaziyat qanday o'zgarishi haqida ko'proq ma'lumot beradi. Ular 10 yoshdan 54 yoshgacha bo'lgan ayollarning tug'ilish darajasi haqidagi so'nggi ma'lumotlarni ko'rib chiqishdi va 2100 yilgacha prognozlar tuzdilar.

Odatda, mamlakat aholisini bir xilda saqlash uchun ayollarning har biri taxminan 2,1 ta farzand ko'rishi kerak. Vollset jamoasi 2050 yilga kelib, ko'pchilik mamlakatlarda tug'ilish darajasi bundan past bo'lishini aniqladi. 2100 yilga kelib, ular deyarli barcha mamlakatlarda bu muammo bo'ladi, deb o'ylashadi.

Shu bilan birga, odamlar uzoqroq yashayapti. Bu shuni anglatadiki, keksa odamlarga va ishlamaydigan boshqalarga g'amxo'rlik qilish uchun ishlaydigan yoshdagi odamlar kamroq. Vegard Skirbekkning aytishicha, biz aholining qarishini to'xtata olmaymiz. Ammo biz o'zgarishni sekinlashtirishga harakat qilishimiz kerak, shunda unga tayyorlana olamiz.

Tug'ilish darajasini oshirish uchun boy mamlakatlar odamlarning farzand ko'rishini osonlashtirishga harakat qilishlari kerak. Masalan, ular odamlarga uy-joy topishda va chaqaloqlarni dunyoga keltirishda yordam berishlari mumkin, deydi Skirbekk.

Mamlakatlar, shuningdek, kichikroq va keksa aholi uchun rejalashtirishlari kerak. Ular ko'proq shifoxonalar qurishlari, transportni yaxshilashlari va kamroq maktablarga ega bo'lishlari kerak, deydi Melinda Mills. Shaharlar odamlarga do'konlar va shifoxonalarga borishga yordam berishga ko'proq e'tibor qaratishi mumkin.

Jennifer Sciubba kompaniyalar keksa odamlarga hatto haftasiga bir necha soat bo'lsa ham ishlashni osonlashtirishlari kerakligini aytdi. Uning aytishicha, biz odamlar yoki ishlaydi yoki yo'q deb o'ylaymiz, lekin bu to'g'ri bo'lishi shart emas.

Biroq, ba'zi mamlakatlarda teskari muammo bo'ladi: tug'ilish darajasi juda yuqori. Tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatadiki, bu 2100 yilda ham to'g'ri bo'ladi. Bu mamlakatlarning aksariyati Afrikada bo'ladi. Ular 2100 yilda tug'ilgan barcha chaqaloqlarning yarmini tashkil qilishi mumkin.

Bu mamlakatlarda ayollarga kontratseptsiya va ta'lim olish imkoniyatini yaxshilash tug'ilish darajasini pasaytirishga yordam berishi mumkin, deydi Sciubba. Tug'ilish darajasi yuqori va daromadlari past bo'lgan mamlakatlardan kelgan odamlar boshqa mamlakatlarga ko'chib o'tishlari mumkin. Bu boyroq mamlakatlarni Afrika odamlari uchun raqobatlashishga majbur qilishi mumkin. Ammo, tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatadiki, bu faqat odamlar immigratsiya haqida boshqacha fikrda bo'lishni boshlasalar ishlaydi.

Hamma uchun yanada barqaror va farovon kelajakni ta'minlash uchun hozir ushbu muammolarni hal qilish muhimdir.

Hukumatlar va tashkilotlar har bir mamlakatning o'ziga xos vaziyatiga mos keladigan yechimlar topish uchun birgalikda ishlashlari kerak. Bunga oilalarni qo'llab-quvvatlaydigan va odamlarga demografik o'zgarishlarga moslashishga yordam beradigan ta'lim, sog'liqni saqlash va ijtimoiy dasturlarga investitsiya kiritish kiradi.

Oxir-oqibat, maqsad - har bir kishi o'z yoshi yoki qaerda yashashidan qat'i nazar, gullab-yashnash imkoniyatiga ega bo'lgan dunyoni yaratishdir. Birgalikda ishlayotganimizda, biz tug'ilish darajasining pasayishi muammolarini yenga olamiz va barchamiz uchun yaxshiroq kelajakni yarata olamiz.
mock_data.translationB2:
Global aholi muammolari haqida o'ylaganimizda, ko'pincha Yer yuzidagi odamlar sonining ortib borayotganiga – hozirda taxminan 8 milliard – va atrof-muhitga ta'sirimizga e'tibor qaratamiz. Ammo, mamlakatlar boyib borgani sari odamlar kamroq farzand ko'rayotgani sababli, kelajakda haqiqiy muammo aholining kamayishi bo'lishi mumkin. Bu jamiyatlar va butun dunyo iqtisodiyotlari uchun jiddiy oqibatlarga olib kelishi mumkin.

Hozirgi tendentsiyalarga asoslanib, mutaxassislar taxminan 25 yildan so'ng ko'pchilik mamlakatlarda (taxminan to'rtdan uch qismida) tug'ilish darajasi hozirgi aholi sonini saqlab qolish uchun juda past bo'lishini bashorat qilmoqda. Bu atrof-muhit uchun ijobiy o'zgarish sifatida ko'rilishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, keksa yoshdagi aholini qo'llab-quvvatlaydigan kichikroq mehnatga layoqatli aholi iqtisodiy jihatdan katta muammo tug'diradi. Bu ham afzalliklari, ham kamchiliklari bo'lgan murakkab vaziyat.

Yangi tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, tug'ilish darajasi past va odatda daromadlari yuqori bo'lgan mamlakatlar, masalan, Yevropaning ko'p qismi va tug'ilish darajasi yuqori va daromadlari past bo'lgan mamlakatlarning kichikroq guruhi, asosan Afrikada, o'rtasida aniq tafovut yuzaga keladi. Demografik tendentsiyalardagi bu farqlanish siyosat va rejalashtirishga turli xil yondashuvlarni talab qiladi.

Sietldagi Vashington universitetining tadqiqotchisi Shteyn Emil Vollsetning so'zlariga ko'ra, "Biz XXI asr davomida misli ko'rilmagan ijtimoiy o'zgarishlarga duch kelmoqdamiz. Dunyo bir vaqtning o'zida ba'zi mamlakatlarda tug'ilishning keskin o'sishi, boshqalarida esa tug'ilishning keskin kamayishi bilan kurashadi". Bu vaziyatning murakkabligini va ehtiyotkorlik bilan rejalashtirish zarurligini ta'kidlaydi.

Ushbu keskin farqlar sharoitida iqtisodiy va ijtimoiy barqarorlikni saqlash shu asrning asosiy vazifasi bo'ladi. Xo'sh, mamlakatlar ushbu demografik o'zgarishga tayyorlanish uchun qanday choralar ko'rishi kerak? Potensial ta'sirlarni ko'rib chiqish va tegishli strategiyalarni ishlab chiqish juda muhimdir.

Global aholining o'sishi uzoq muddatli tendentsiyasi atrof-muhit bilan bog'liq xavotirlarni uyg'otgan bo'lsa-da, demograflar bu o'sish abadiy davom etmasligini doimo bilishgan. Taxminlar har xil, ammo biz 2060 va 2080 yillar oralig'ida "aholining eng yuqori cho'qqisiga" – global aholi soni 9,5 dan 10 milliardgacha yetib, shundan so'ng kamayishni boshlash yo'lida ekanmiz. Aholi o'sishining bu barqarorlashuvi muhim burilish nuqtasidir.

Vollset jamoasining so'nggi prognozlari global tendentsiyalar bo'yicha Birlashgan Millatlar Tashkiloti kabi tashkilotlarning avvalgi bashoratlari bilan asosan mos keladi. Biroq, yangi tadqiqotlar tug'ilish darajasi bo'yicha eng so'nggi ma'lumotlarga asoslanib, 10 yoshdan 54 yoshgacha bo'lgan besh yillik yosh guruhlari uchun 2100 yilgacha bo'lgan davrda mamlakatdan mamlakatga qanday o'zgarishini batafsil tahlil qiladi. Ushbu darajadagi tafsilot samarali rejalashtirish uchun juda muhimdir.

Mamlakatlarga odatda aholisini barqaror saqlash uchun har bir ayolga 2,1 nafar bola tug'ilishi kerak. Vollset jamoasi 2050 yilga kelib tug'ilish darajasi mamlakatlarning 76 foizida ushbu darajadan pastga tushishini aniqladi. 2100 yilga kelib, bu ko'rsatkich 97 foizga yetishi bashorat qilinmoqda. Tug'ilish darajasining bunday keng tarqalgan pasayishi ko'plab davlatlar uchun jiddiy muammo tug'diradi.

Shu bilan birga, odamlar uzoqroq umr ko'rishmoqda, ya'ni aholida keksa odamlarni va ishlamaydigan boshqalarni qo'llab-quvvatlaydigan kamroq mehnatga layoqatli odamlar bor. Oslo shahridagi Norvegiya jamoat salomatligi institutidan Vegard Skirbekkning so'zlariga ko'ra, aholining qarishi muqarrar. "Biroq, bu jarayonga yaxshiroq tayyorgarlik ko'rish uchun o'tishni sekinlashtirishga harakat qilish kerak". Sekin o'tishni tez o'tishdan ko'ra boshqarish osonroq.

Tug'ilish darajasining pasayishini sekinlashtirish uchun daromadi yuqori bo'lgan mamlakatlar odamlarga ko'proq farzand ko'rishni osonlashtirish va jozibaliroq qilishga harakat qilishlari kerak. Bu arzon uy-joy va fertilizatsiya davolash usullaridan foydalanishni yaxshilashni o'z ichiga olishi mumkin, deydi Skirbekk. Qo'llab-quvvatlovchi siyosatlar o'zgarishlarga olib kelishi mumkin.

Mamlakatlar, shuningdek, kasalxonalarni ko'proq qurish, transport tizimlarini yaxshilash va ehtimol kamroq maktablarga ega bo'lish orqali aholining qisqarishi va qarishi uchun rejalashtirishlari kerak, deydi Oksford universitetidan Melinda Mills. "Shaharlar odamlarni maktablarga va ishga olib borishga e'tibor qaratmoqda. Ular ularni do'konlar va kasalxonalarga olib borishga ko'proq e'tibor qaratishlari mumkin", deydi u. Infrastruktura o'zgaruvchan demografiyaga moslashishi kerak.

Vashingtondagi (AQSh) "Wilson Center" tahlil markazidan Jennifer Sciubba kompaniyalar keksa odamlarga ishda uzoqroq qolishni osonlashtirishlari kerakligini, ehtimol qisqartirilgan soatlarni taklif qilish orqali taklif qilmoqda. "Bizda yoki ishlaysiz yoki yo'q degan ikkilik qarash bor, ammo bu shunday bo'lishi shart emas", deydi u. Moslashuvchan ish tartibi tajribali ishchilarni saqlab qolishga yordam beradi.

Biroq, ozchilik mamlakatlar teskari muammoga duch kelmoqdalar: tug'ilish darajasi 2,1 o'rnini bosish darajasidan yuqori. Yangi tadqiqot shuni ko'rsatadiki, bu 2100 yilda ham shunday bo'lishi mumkin. Ushbu mamlakatlarning aksariyati Sahroi Kabir janubiy Afrikada joylashgan bo'lib, 2100 yilda tug'ilgan barcha bolalarning yarmini tashkil qilishi prognoz qilinmoqda. Ushbu mintaqalardagi demografik muammolar juda xilma-xildir.

Ushbu tug'ilish darajasi yuqori bo'lgan mamlakatlarda qizlar uchun kontratseptsiyadan foydalanishni yaxshilash va ta'lim berish tug'ilish darajasini pasaytirishga yordam berishi ko'rsatilgan, deydi Sciubba. Tug'ilish darajasi yuqori, daromadi past bo'lgan mamlakatlardan migratsiya ham davom etishi mumkin, bu esa boyroq mamlakatlarning Sahroi Kabir janubiy Afrikadan kelgan muhojirlar uchun raqobatlashishiga olib kelishi mumkin, deyiladi tadqiqot mualliflari. "Biroq, bu yondashuv faqat immigratsiyaga nisbatan hozirgi jamoatchilik va siyosiy munosabatlar o'zgargan taqdirdagina ishlaydi", deyishadi ular. Migratsiyani samarali boshqarish uchun munosabat va siyosatni o'zgartirish muhim bo'ladi.
mock_data.translationC1: Bu hududlarda, Sciubba ta'kidlaganidek, kontratseptsiya va qizlar uchun ta'lim olish imkoniyatining oshishi tug'ilish darajasini kamaytirishda samarali ekanligi isbotlangan. Bundan tashqari, tug'ilish darajasi yuqori va daromadi past bo'lgan mamlakatlardan migratsiya davom etishi kutilmoqda, bu esa Sahroi Kabirdan janubiy Afrikadan kelgan migrantlar uchun boyroq davlatlar o'rtasida raqobatning kuchayishiga olib kelishi mumkin. Biroq, tadqiqot mualliflari bunday yondashuvning muvaffaqiyati immigratsiyaga nisbatan jamoatchilik va siyosiy munosabatlarda tubdan o'zgarishga bog'liq ekanligini ta'kidlaydilar. Migratsiyaning afzalliklari va qiyinchiliklarini chuqurroq tushunish inklyuziv va barqaror jamiyatlarni rivojlantirish uchun juda muhimdir.
